**Lifted-data map (§9.4 Ford circles; Lean-verified, FF-3; shared library v23).** For lifted rosette data $(t_1,t_2,s,n_3)$ with $t_1,t_2\in\mathbb Z$, $s\in\mathbb Q$ and $n_3\ge 1$, the map $\Phi(t_1,t_2,s,n_3)=C(x)$ sends the record to the Ford circle at its Ford address $x=t_2s/n_3$. With phase address $a=t_1s-x=k_1s/n_3$ (the $z_1$ phase of Rmk II.5a, $\theta_1=\pi a$) and amplitude $r>0$, the phasor $r\,e^{i\pi a}$ lies on the real axis ($\operatorname{Im}=0$) iff $a\in\mathbb Z$. This extends the contact identity of Rmk II.5a from integer to rational $s$, and it is unchanged for $n_6<0$, whose point $-\bar z$ has the same imaginary part. On the shells $n_3=N$ with $t_1=t_2=1$, for $N=2,\dots,B+1$ ($B\ge1$), the real-axis events with $s\in[0,N]$ are exactly $s=mN/(N-1)$, $0\le m\le N-1$, with addresses $m/(N-1)$; the deduplicated address set is the Farey set $F_B$, and consecutive members $p/q<p'/q'$ satisfy $qp'-pq'=1$. Along a finite address path, each edge is exactly one of tangent (determinant $\pm1$), stall (equal addresses) or break, and every tangent edge carries an exact rational kiss point lying on both circles. $\Phi$ is defined on lifted data, not on phasor values: at $N=3$, $s=0$ and $s=3$ give the same phasor and the addresses $0$ and $1$. Oriented or continuous Ford-circle arcs, a map from unlabelled phasor values or paths, and any dynamical correspondence are not defined; that comparison remains interpretive only.
